title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomic profiling of cultured cells and engineered tissues
author: Helms, Bertassoni

This section details the steps to perform hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. Immediately following staining, a high resolution, stitched image will be taken of the entire slide. Currently, Visium HD is offered for a 6.5 x 6.5 mm capture area. Only one 6.5 x 6.5 mm region of a microscope slide can be transferred. It is important that the imaging aligns with what will be sequenced, as this image will be imported into the sequencing alignment pipeline (Space Ranger) and used during data analysis. We therefore recommend oversampling during image (i.e., image the majority of the slide) and create the cropped region of interest image that aligns with the CytAssist image before running Space Ranger. Please consult 10x Genomics, Visium HD Spatial Applications Imaging Guidelines Technical Note (CG000688) for additional imaging guidance.Note: Immunofluorescence (IF) can also be performed on the sample prior to H&E staining. Please be aware, depending on the integrity of your 2D culture/tissue and the adhesion to the slide, the extra liquid exchanges of the IF protocol may increase likelihood of sample detachment. Refer to 10× Genomics, Visium HD Fixed Frozen Tissue Preparation Handbook (CG000764), Section 3, for detailed instructions, including approved reagents, to perform IF.CRITICAL: Be extra gentle during liquid exchanges to prevent sample detachment. Never touch the sample; it is better to have a little excess liquid remaining on the sample than to disturb/damage the sample trying to remove all liquid.31.Set up seven 1,000 mL beakers, each filled with 800 mL Milli-Q or UltraPure water. Do not touch the section! Some remaining water is okay.41.Return the slide to a flat, clean, nonabsorbent work surface.42.Add 1 mL bluing buffer onto the slide to uniformly cover the sample.43.Incubate for 1 min at room temperature.44.Remove bluing buffer by tilting the slide over a discard jar (i.e. 50 mL conical tube) and gently tap the edge of the slide to a lint-free laboratory wipe to remove excess.45.Immerse the slide into Water Beaker #4 and gently dunk 15 times.46.Gently tap the edge of the slide onto a lint-free laboratory wipe and wipe excess water from the back of the slide. Do not touch the section! steps.title: Expand cells for experiment
steps.instruction: Culture and expand the selected cell lines according to their standard protocols. For single‑cell bioprinting, harvest 1–2 × 10⁶ cells of each cell type to ensure sufficient material for downstream handling.

steps.title: Prepare collagen‑coated slide
steps.instruction: Sterile‑technique preparation of a microscope slide coated with PureCol collagen for cell seeding.

substeps.instruction: Clean all surfaces with 70 % ethanol and keep containers capped when not in use.
In a biosafety cabinet, transfer one sterilized microscope slide into a 100 mm petri dish.
Pipette ~750 µL of prepared PureCol collagen solution onto the centre of the slide, spreading gently with a pipette tip to cover the entire viable region.
Incubate the slide at room temperature for 2 h (do not exceed 3 h to avoid drying and flaking).
Add 1× PBS to the dish along the wall until the slide is fully submerged (~25 mL).
Aspirate the PBS carefully without disturbing the coated slide; repeat the PBS wash two more times for a total of three washes.
Add ~25 mL 1× PBS again to keep the slide covered and prevent dehydration.
Using sterile forceps, place a second sterile microscope slide at an angle in the dish to hold the coated slide in place.
Aspirate the PBS and replace it with complete cell‑culture medium (add 2 µL Primocin per mL of medium, or as recommended for the cell type).
Cover the dish and incubate at 37 °C while harvesting the cells.

steps.title: Seed cells onto coated slide
steps.instruction: After the slide has been prepared and placed in complete medium, seed the expanded cells onto the collagen‑coated surface using standard cell‑culture techniques and incubate at 37 °C until ready for staining.

steps.title: Hematoxylin‑Eosin staining and imaging
steps.instruction: Perform H&E staining on the cultured slide, mount with glycerol, and acquire a high‑resolution bright‑field image of the entire capture area.

substeps.instruction: Set up seven 1 L beakers, each containing 800 mL Milli‑Q or UltraPure water; label them 1–7.
Remove the slide from PBS, tap the edge onto a lint‑free laboratory wipe to remove excess liquid (do not touch the sample).
Place the slide on a flat, clean, non‑absorbent surface.
Add 1 mL hematoxylin to cover the sample uniformly; incubate 1 min at room temperature.
Tilt the slide over a discard jar, remove hematoxylin, and tap the edge onto a lint‑free wipe.
Immerse the slide in Water Beaker #1 and gently dunk 5 times.
Immerse in Water Beaker #2 and gently dunk 15 times.
Immerse in Water Beaker #3 and gently dunk 15 times.
Tap the edge onto a lint‑free wipe; some water may remain on the back of the slide.
Add 1 mL bluing buffer to cover the sample; incubate 1 min at room temperature.
Remove bluing buffer as above and dunk the slide in Water Beaker #4 for 15 gentle dunks.
Tap the edge onto a lint‑free wipe.
Add 1 mL fresh (undiluted) eosin; incubate 1 min at room temperature.
Remove eosin as above; immerse in Water Beaker #5 for 30 seconds.
Dunk in Water Beaker #6 for 10 gentle dunks.
Tap the edge onto a lint‑free wipe; do not air‑dry the slide.
Using a P1000 tip, dispense 100–150 µL of 85 % glycerol mounting medium over the sample, avoiding bubbles.
Slowly lower a coverslip from one end, laying it flat without introducing bubbles; wick away excess mounting medium with a lint‑free wipe if needed.
Immediately image the slide at 20–40× bright‑field magnification, following 10x Genomics imaging guidelines.
After imaging, immerse the slide (long edge parallel to the beaker bottom) in Water Beaker #7 until the coverslip detaches and falls off.
Dunk the slide in Water Beaker #7 30 times to remove residual mounting medium.
Tap the edge onto a lint‑free wipe; some water may remain.
Air‑dry the slide for 5 min.
Place the slide on a low‑profile thermocycler adapter with the lid open and incubate 3 min at 37 °C.
Proceed directly to destaining.

steps.title: Destain and decrosslink tissue
steps.instruction: Follow the Visium HD Fixed Frozen Tissue Preparation Handbook (CG000764, Rev C) to perform all destaining (Section 2.6) and decrosslinking (Section 2.7) steps as described.

steps.title: Process sequencing data with Space Ranger
steps.instruction: Run the 10x Genomics Space Ranger pipeline on the generated FASTQ files together with required inputs.

substeps.instruction: Gather the following inputs: FASTQ files, reference transcriptome, probe set, H&E (or IF) image, CytAssist image, slide number, and capture area.
Place all files in a single folder with clear names and no spaces.
Execute Space Ranger (v3.1.3) locally (e.g., via Windows Subsystem for Linux) or on the 10x Genomics cloud, providing the inputs above.
After completion, inspect the web summary and metrics .csv file.
If needed, manually align the H&E and CytAssist images in Loupe Browser before finalizing the run.

steps.title: Annotate barcodes and downstream analysis
steps.instruction: Use Loupe Browser and Seurat (or equivalent) to annotate cell barcodes and perform downstream analyses.

substeps.instruction: Open the 8 µm‑binned .cloupe file in Loupe Browser; create custom groups with the selection tool and export all barcodes (including unlabeled).
Load the Space Ranger outputs into Seurat (v5); import the Loupe custom groupings as metadata for the Seurat object.
Proceed with downstream analyses using tools such as Seurat, Squidpy, or other preferred packages.
